title: Machine-learning X-ray analysis provides bulk evidence for a Bragg-glass phase in PdₓErTe₃
summary: Researchers combined extensive X-ray diffraction with X-ray Temperature Clustering (X-TEC) to identify Bragg-glass signatures in the charge-density-wave material PdₓErTe₃. Their analysis extracted diffraction features across about 20,000 Brillouin zones and found a diverging correlation length and a phase diagram consistent with a Bragg-glass transition. The result provides bulk diffraction evidence for a phase that had been difficult to establish experimentally.
ai_technology: X-ray Temperature Clustering (X-TEC), a machine-learning analysis of X-ray diffraction peaks
organization: Cornell University; Stanford University; Argonne National Laboratory; University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign

evidence.tested: Researchers combined extensive X-ray diffraction with X-ray Temperature Clustering (X-TEC) to identify Bragg-glass signatures in the charge-density-wave material PdₓErTe₃.
evidence.unknown: The authors frame the result as evidence for the Bragg-glass phase based on characteristic diffraction behavior, rather than direct imaging of all underlying defects. Machine learning enabled the scale of peak extraction; physical interpretation and measurements were done by the team.
evidence.ai_role: Automatically extracted and clustered charge-density-wave diffraction peaks across temperature and momentum, enabling high-throughput estimation of peak spread/correlation length from a large set of Brillouin zones; researchers interpreted these features as evidence for Bragg-glass order.
